name: face-blur
desc: Free, open-source face anonymizer for Windows — blur or pixelate faces in photos and videos locally. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **Photos and videos** — faces detected and blurred frame by frame in clips, not just stills
✅ **Tracking between frames** — a blur box follows a face through motion instead of flickering off
✅ **Blur or pixelate** — strength dial per mode, with a solid-cover option for strict cases
✅ **Keep-list** — mark the presenter's face to stay sharp while everyone else is covered
✅ **Batch photo folders** — a thousand event photos anonymized unattended
✅ **Copy-first workflow** — originals untouched; outputs written to a separate folder with a manifest
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime and detection model bundled, portable, offline, MIT
compare: | Feature | **face-blur** | YouTube blur tool | Manual editing | Cloud anonymizers |
| Price | **Free, MIT** | Built-in upload | Subscription | Paid tiers |
| Works on local files | **Yes** | Upload required | Yes | Upload
| Batch photo folders | **Yes** | No | No | Partial
| Keep-list for target faces | **Yes** | Partial | Manual | No
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Browser | Installer | Browser
faqQ: blur faces in videos and photos offline on Windows?
faqA: Editors charge subscriptions, web tools want the footage uploaded and YouTube's blur only exists after posting. face-blur detects and tracks faces locally, keeps chosen faces sharp and covers the rest in batch. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline, originals untouched.
s1: Dark anonymizer (#121417, zinc #71717A): video preview with tracked blur boxes on three faces, keep-list chip on the presenter, strength dial at 0.8.
s2: Photo batch: 240 event photos with detected face counts, blur mode tiles, progress at 61 percent, manifest checkbox enabled.
s3: Track review: timeline strip with follow segments per face, two manual keyframe dots added, export button, output folder chip.
